title: The generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) and its application for ground state search

metadata.authors: Nakaji, Kouhei; Kristensen, Lasse Bjørn; Campos-Gonzalez-Angulo, Jorge A.; Vakili, Mohammad Ghazi; Huang, Haozhe; Bagherimehrab, Mohsen; Gorgulla, Christoph; Wong, FuTe; McCaskey, Alex; Kim, Jin-Sung; Nguyen, Thien; Rao, Pooja; Aspuru-Guzik, Alan

source_summary: The generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) is a new approach that uses classical generative models, specifically a transformer-based GPT quantum eigensolver (GPT-QE), to optimize quantum circuits for simulating ground states of electronic structure Hamiltonians, with potential applications in broader areas of quantum computing.
abstract: We introduce the generative quantum eigensolver (GQE), a novel method for applying classical generative models for quantum simulation. The GQE algorithm optimizes a classical generative model to produce quantum circuits with desired properties. Here, we develop a transformer-based implementation, which we name the generative pre-trained transformer-based (GPT) quantum eigensolver (GPT-QE), leveraging both pre-training on existing datasets and training without any prior knowledge. We demonstrate the effectiveness of training and pre-training GPT-QE in the search for ground states of electronic structure Hamiltonians. GQE strategies can extend beyond the problem of Hamiltonian simulation into other application areas of quantum computing.

methods.value: The authors propose a transformer-based implementation of GQE, named GPT-QE, and demonstrate its training and pretraining on electronic structure Hamiltonians, comparing its performance to coupled cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) methods.

problems.value: Developing a quantum computational framework that operates outside the variational quantum algorithm paradigm by applying classical generative models to quantum simulation for ground state search.

hypotheses.value: A generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) can optimize a classical generative model to produce quantum circuits with desired properties, potentially overcoming limitations of variational quantum algorithms.

evidence.value: GPT-QE outperforms CCSD in the strong bond dissociation regime of the nitrogen molecule and approaches chemical accuracy, as shown in Figures 4, 5, and 6.

conclusions.value: GPT-QE demonstrates the ability to find a quantum state with energy close to that of the ground state, offering a new approach to quantum circuit generation that leverages classical generative models.

failure_paths.value: success: Comparing GRPO and Logit Matching loss functions for N2 at bond length 1.5 ˚A. Evidence: GRPO consistently outperforms Logit Matching across all gate counts, achieving lower energy values and demonstrating better convergence properties.

success: Investigating the effect of pre-training data ratio on energy evaluation count for N2 at bond length 1.05 ˚A. Evidence: Using pre-constructed data significantly reduces the number of energy evaluations needed to achieve chemical accuracy.

success: Validating the practical applicability of GPT-QE on the IBM 127-qubit backend for the H2 molecule. Evidence: Calculations performed on ibm kawasaki closely reproduce the exact energy values, demonstrating successful training on the quantum device.
